requirements.evidence: Covers every contract item. Migration has owner_seq storedAs("CASE WHEN role = 'owner' THEN 1 ELSE NULL END") plus a unique index 'entity_memberships_one_owner', and the slug and membership unique indexes use the names the task gives. The models, enum manageable(), User::membershipFor, factories with owner/admin/employee states and both policies all match. EntityPickController::pick returns 403 for non-members before touching the session, writes Log::channel('audit') and redirects to the dashboard. Each Livewire page authorizes in mount(). Members::assignRole validates role against Rule::in(manageable()). Members::removeMember blocks the owner (policy) and the last manager (otherManagers === 0 -> 403). Settings::transfer re-checks the owner and target with lockForUpdate inside a transaction and demotes before it promotes. Settings::delete clears the session only when it is the current entity. The dashboard wraps the settings link and owner notice in @can('manageSettings'). The routes and both locales' lang keys match.

conventions.evidence: Policies handle authorization, the migrations have down() methods, $fillable is set through #[Fillable], docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated, existing <x-form-field>/<x-button> components are reused, and Pint-style PHPDoc is present. The clear deviation: the conventions say 'Domain writes go through app/Actions/*', but addMember, assignRole, removeMember, save, delete and transfer all write straight from the Livewire components (Members.php:47, Settings.php:43, Settings.php:53-56, Settings.php:94-96). Settings uses a rules() method rather than #[Validate], which the security policy allows but differs from the stated #[Validate] pattern. docs/business-rules.md is not updated for the new invariants (no owner removal, last-manager rule).

security.evidence: Every public action calls $this->authorize(...) (Members.php:36,59,77; Settings.php:39,51,67). $entity is #[Locked] on all three components, and a test covers the entity-swap tamper. Members::resolveMembership scopes action parameters to the bound entity (Members.php:104-110). transfer re-resolves the target and checks entity, role and caller inside a locked transaction. Blade output uses only {{ }}, and mass assignment is restricted. Small gaps: Settings::$targetMembershipId is a public, untyped property with no #[Validate] rule; filter_var plus the 403 path limits the impact. No rate limiting on member add or transfer (low impact).

tests.evidence: Seven Pest files. EntityMembersTest covers the happy path, duplicate and unknown email, employee 403 on add/assign, owner role rejected, owner not demotable, self-removal, last manager, and cross-entity tamper. EntitySettingsTest covers save, own-slug, unique slug, required name, delete with session cleared/untouched, and transfer to admin/employee/other-entity/self/vanished owner, plus the 'bound entity cannot be swapped' test. Also EntityPickTest (audit log mocked, session untouched on 403), EntityPolicyTest, EntityPagesTest (settings URL hidden for non-owners, 403 with session pointing elsewhere, guest/unverified redirects) and DB-level second-owner rejection in EntityTest.

simplicity.evidence: Lean overall: a small pick controller, one shared resolveMembership helper and isTransferableAdmin. Minor duplication: the manages() helper is copied in EntityPolicy and EntityMembershipPolicy, and the owner/admin check is repeated as whereIn([Owner, Admin]) in Members::removeMember. transfer validates the target twice (before and inside the transaction); this is defensible for the race but adds code.

readability.evidence: Clear names, short methods, PHPDoc on public and protected helpers, and a comment explaining demote-before-promote (Settings.php:93) and the generated column (migration). Untyped `public $targetMembershipId = null;` stands out against the typed siblings. Views use a fully qualified \App\Models\UserRole::Owner inline in members.blade.php.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, migrations, factories, policies, the pick controller, three Livewire pages with views, routes, lang keys, docs and tests. No onboarding, switcher, session-guard middleware, locale middleware or navbar changes.

issues.explanation: Domain writes (add/assign/remove member, update/delete entity, transfer ownership) happen directly in Livewire components instead of in app/Actions/* use-case classes, as the project conventions require.
Public client-writable $targetMembershipId is untyped and has no #[Validate] rule; it relies only on filter_var plus a 403, not on declared validation as the Livewire policy requires.

New domain invariants (owner cannot be removed, last manager cannot be removed, transfer only to an admin) are not reflected in business-rules.md, although the 'keep docs in sync' convention asks for it.
The owner/admin manages() helper is duplicated across both policies.
Fully qualified \App\Models\UserRole::Owner comparison in the view, while the policy could already hide these buttons.
Sensitive actions (adding members, ownership transfer) have no RateLimiter, which the Livewire policy recommends.

review.summary: The change implements the entity data model with a portable DB-enforced single owner, both policies, the pick endpoint with audit logging, and the Dashboard/Members/Settings Livewire pages. Every action is authorized server-side, the entity is locked and transfer is atomic, and the tests are thorough, including tamper and unauthorized cases. The main deviation is that domain writes live in the components instead of app/Actions; with a few small validation and doc gaps, I would approve it with follow-ups rather than as is.
